description: A heap block larger than SIZE_TABLE's last entry (~7 MiB, runtime/src/heap/block_pool.rs) is allocated at its exact size and freed to the system allocator after the collection that empties it. On macOS that memory stays resident: in the fz-9x7.8 round-5 F variant on the full distiller trace, vmmap at peak showed MALLOC_LARGE (empty) 4.0 GB virtual / 2.5 GB resident, and peak RSS was 4.8 GB against a heap of at most 1.18 GB (from-space plus copied). Each major at a different heap size leaves its own freed large blocks behind. Repro and data: session scratchpad 9x7-8/prof/vmmap-F.txt, tel5/dist-full-*.jsonl. Experiment first: measure RSS after repeated majors at growing heap sizes, with and without the exact-size path.

comments.text: Rescoped per the approved GC memory plan v3 (https://claude.ai/artifact/Pqqu5yTcQdBbkGsZyZiykb): blocks above the pool come from mmap segments with BEAM's 10-entry segment cache, munmap past it. fz has no global allocator and no mmap/madvise/munmap today; blocks above 7,391,280 B are exact calloc/free. Blocked by fz-9x7.21 (no zeroing) and fz-9x7.22 (mimalloc experiment, which decides whether fz code is needed).

title: A heap block above the pool's largest size comes from a mapped segment; a freed one is cached or unmapped
